reading.body:
Frank Pallone's AI record is mostly money and votes: $30,000 from tech and AI-focused PACs, and five recorded votes on AI-related bills, all Yea.

The pattern is that the contributions and the votes run in parallel rather than in sequence. Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Intel PACs gave across 2025 and 2026, and the recorded votes on H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, S. 146, and H.R. 7757 fall in the same window. The data does not establish that any contribution preceded or produced any vote, and the page says so directly. What it does establish is that the same member is receiving money from the largest compute buyers and voting on the legislation that governs what those companies build.

For AI specifically, the money is coming from the companies whose data centers and models are the subject of the bills. Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Intel are not generic tech donors here, they are the firms whose compute buildout is the constraint on AI scaling. The bills named in the cosponsorship entry are child safety and online protection measures, not grid or data center legislation, so this record does not show Pallone acting on the power and siting questions that determine how fast AI can grow.

What the data does not cover is large. It holds 13 events, all dated, with no committee assignments, no floor speeches, no positions on permitting, transmission, or energy, and no spending by the member. It also does not show contributions from utilities, independent power producers, or data center developers, which are the actors closest to the binding constraint. A reader should treat this as a money-and-votes ledger for one member, not as a measure of influence over AI policy.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Frank Pallone: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
